title: B1 · L13 — Defining relative clauses
description: Oraciones relativas especificativas con who, which, that, whose y where para añadir información esencial que define al sustantivo.

questions.prompt: Le describes a un visitante quién vive al lado.
questions.question: Complete: 'The woman ___ lives next door is a nurse.'
questions.explanation: 'Who' → pronombre relativo para PERSONAS como sujeto de la oración relativa. 'That' también sirve para personas de forma informal. Error típico del hispanohablante: usar 'which' (que se traduce como 'que' pero solo va con cosas/animales) o 'what' (que no existe como relativo aquí).
examples: The man who called me this morning is my uncle. → persona + verbo
The teacher who helped us with the project is Mr. Brown. → persona sujeto

questions.prompt: Describes un libro que compraste recientemente.
questions.question: Choose: 'The book ___ I bought is really interesting.'
questions.explanation: 'Which' → cosas, objetos, animales. También vale 'that' (más informal). Cuando el relativo es OBJETO (aquí 'I bought THE BOOK'), se puede OMITIR: 'The book I bought'. Error típico: usar 'who' con objetos porque 'que' vale para todo en español.
examples: The house which we visited last weekend is over 200 years old. → objeto + relativa
The dog which barks loudest at night is mine, unfortunately. → animal + relativa

questions.statement: In defining relative clauses, we can omit 'who' or 'which' when they are the object of the clause.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Regla clave: si el relativo funciona como OBJETO de la oración relativa, se puede omitir. 'The film (which) I watched' → objeto (yo la vi) → OMISIBLE. 'The film that inspired me' → sujeto (la película inspiró) → NO omisible.
examples: The book (that) I read was fantastic. → 'that' omisible (objeto)
The book that inspired me is over there. → 'that' obligatorio (sujeto)

questions.text: The restaurant that we went to last night had amazing food.
questions.explanation: Nota que la preposición 'to' se queda al FINAL en inglés natural (no 'to which we went'). Esto es típico del habla real. 'That' aquí es OMISIBLE en habla informal: 'The restaurant we went to...'. Se pronuncia con muy poco énfasis, casi imperceptible.
examples: The hotel (that) we stayed at was excellent — highly recommend. → preposición al final
The person (that) I spoke to was really kind. → mismo patrón, 'that' omisible

questions.prompt: Señalas a alguien famoso y explicas su familia.
questions.question: Complete: 'That's the girl ___ father is a famous singer.'
questions.explanation: 'Whose' → posesión en oraciones relativas. Sustituye a 'her father', 'his father', 'their father' etc. Error típico del hispanohablante: usar 'who's' (contracción de 'who is', ¡no posesivo!) o 'who' que no expresa posesión.
examples: The man whose car was stolen called the police. → posesión de un objeto
The student whose essay won the prize is over there. → posesión de una obra

questions.prompt: Empareja cada pronombre relativo con su uso:
questions.explanation: Cuatro pronombres relativos básicos: 'who' (personas), 'which' (cosas/animales), 'that' (comodín informal para ambos), 'whose' (posesión). Además, 'where' (lugares) y 'when' (tiempos) también se usan como relativos. En habla informal 'that' desplaza a 'who/which' con frecuencia.
examples: The man who called me left a message. → persona sujeto
The book which I bought is on the table. → objeto sujeto

questions.prompt: Le muestras a un amigo la ciudad de tu infancia.
questions.question: Choose: 'This is the town ___ I grew up.'
questions.explanation: 'Where' → relativo para LUGARES. Sustituye a 'in which', 'at which'. Error típico: usar 'which' + verbo intransitivo ('the town which I grew up') que suena raro; o mantener 'in' al final ('the town which I grew up in') que también funciona pero 'where' es más limpio.
examples: This is the house where I was born, actually. → lugar de origen
That's the little shop where I buy my coffee every morning. → lugar habitual

questions.target: Honestly, the person who inspired me the most was my grandmother — she was incredible.
questions.explanation: Situación: hablas de tu heroína personal en una conversación profunda. Relativa definidora con 'who' + sujeto. 'Honestly' + cierre emocional 'she was incredible' añaden autenticidad. Fórmula típica para hablar de referentes vitales.
examples: The teacher who changed my life was Mr. Smith — I still remember his classes. → figura clave
The friend who helped me most through everything is Ana, hands down. → apoyo esencial

questions.statement: Defining relative clauses use commas to separate them from the main sentence.
questions.explanation: FALSO. Las relativas DEFINIDORAS (especificativas) NO llevan comas porque la información es ESENCIAL para identificar el sustantivo. Las relativas NO DEFINIDORAS (explicativas) sí llevan comas porque añaden info extra prescindible. Regla mental: sin comas = necesario; con comas = extra.
examples: Defining: The man who lives here is my friend. → sin comas, info esencial
Non-defining: My father, who lives here, is 70. → con comas, info extra

questions.prompt: Identifica la frase correcta sobre una película que viste.
questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The film who I watched was boring.
The film which I watched was boring.
The film whose I watched was boring.
The film where I watched was boring.
questions.explanation: 'Film' es una COSA → 'which' (o 'that'). Errores: (A) 'who' es para personas; (C) 'whose' expresa posesión, no encaja aquí; (D) 'where' es para lugares. Este error confunde mucho a hispanohablantes porque 'que' en español sirve para todo.
examples: The song which she wrote became a huge hit. → cosa (canción)
The film that we saw last night was absolutely amazing. → cosa (película)

questions.text: The people who live in that flat are always very friendly and helpful.
questions.explanation: Nota el linking 'who-live' y 'in-that' fluidos. 'Are' con weak form /ə/ casi imperceptible. 'Who' introduce info ESENCIAL — sin ella no sabemos a qué personas se refiere. Estructura clásica de descripción: [sustantivo] + who + [características].
examples: The students who study hard usually succeed in life. → generalización
The neighbours who moved in last month are absolutely lovely. → descripción concreta

questions.prompt: Hablas de las vacaciones típicas del año en tu país.
questions.question: Complete: 'This is the time of year ___ many people go on holiday.'
questions.explanation: 'When' → relativo para MOMENTOS temporales (year, month, day, moment, time). Sustituye a 'at which', 'in which'. Error típico: usar 'where' (lugar) o 'which' (cosas) por analogía con el español 'en el que'.
examples: Summer is the season when we travel most. → estación + when
August is the month when many shops close in Europe. → mes + when

questions.statement: 'That' can replace both 'who' and 'which' in defining relative clauses.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'That' funciona como comodín informal tanto para personas ('the man that called') como para cosas ('the car that broke down') en relativas DEFINIDORAS. Ojo: 'that' NO se usa en relativas NO definidoras (las de comas).
examples: The man that called me = the man who called me. → equivalentes
The car that broke down = the car which broke down. → mismo significado

questions.prompt: Comentas sobre una decisión sorprendente de una compañera.
questions.question: Choose: 'The reason ___ she left is unclear.'
questions.explanation: 'Why' funciona como relativo casi EXCLUSIVAMENTE con 'reason'. Es un uso limitado pero muy natural. Alternativas: 'The reason that she left' o 'The reason she left' (omitiendo el relativo). 'Which' sería raro; 'where' es lugar.
examples: That's the reason why I called you last night. → causa explicada
Do you know the reason why he was so angry? → curiosidad sobre la causa

questions.target: The city where I was born has changed a lot in the last ten years, honestly — I barely recognise it.
questions.explanation: Situación: hablas de tus orígenes y cómo ha evolucionado. Relativa con 'where' + lugar + verbo compuesto ('has changed'). Discourse marker 'honestly' + cierre vívido 'I barely recognise it' añaden autenticidad. Muy útil para hablar de la transformación de sitios personales.
examples: The village where I grew up is really quite small, only about 500 people. → lugar de origen
The country where I lived last year is stunning — I miss it. → lugar reciente
